_comment: THE ROOT CAPABILITY, and the largest assumption in the entire ladder.
This record is what the user's trigger mints: the authority the whole chain may
spend on one goal. It is loaded by common/chaind/chaind.py, which runs on the host
and is bind-mounted into no sandbox, and it is assigned to the first hop at startup.
It is HAND-WRITTEN. Nothing in this repo translates "investigate why service X is
slow and fix its config" into the key list below. Add auth_disabled to that list,
or drop the keys constraint entirely, and every check rung 4 performs still passes
while the attack succeeds -- attenuation is exactly as good as the thing being
attenuated. Who writes this record from a natural-language goal is a backlog item,
and a reviewer should ask about it. See rung4/README.md, "Threat model delta".
The three keys are the ones a latency investigation would plausibly need to change.
auth_disabled is not one of them, and that single absence is what rung 4 enforces.
